title: Bibliometric analysis and visualization of top papers in dentistry from 2012 to 2022 based on essential science indicators
authors: Taghdisi kashani, Amene; Batooli, Zahra; Mozafari, Mostafa
abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:sec><jats:title>Objectives</jats:title><jats:p>This study aims to analyze and visualize the top dental papers from 2012 to 2022 using data from essential science indicators (ESIs).</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Materials and Methods</jats:title><jats:p>The present study was conducted using library and retrospective bibliometric analysis methods. Additionally, a science map has been created. Web of Science was searched on January 18, 2023. The results were limited to the top papers in ESIs. The bibliometric information of the top papers was evaluated. Next, the VOSviewer was used to perform a co‐occurrence analysis and visualize data.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Results</jats:title><jats:p>The findings showed that <jats:italic>Mariano Belén Sanz</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Maurizio S. Tonetti</jats:italic> were the top two authors. The University of London and the University of Bern had the highest number of articles. These articles were published in 55 journals. According to the analysis of keyword co‐occurrence, the most frequently used keywords in the field of dentistry include “periodontitis,” “dental implants,” “periodontal disease,” “mechanical properties,” “peri‐implantitis,” “oral health,” “dental caries,” “dental materials,” “3D printing.”</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title><jats:p>The findings of this study enable readers to pinpoint the authors, organizations, countries, and journals that have made the biggest contributions to the list of the most often cited dentistry papers. In medicine, bibliometric citation analysis is frequently used to assist researchers in learning the fundamentals of a subject and pinpoint subtopics of broad interest for additional study.</jats:p></jats:sec>
